en: Of Joltoy beyond measure,
His stature like a plane tree,
[His prowess like a falcon's,]
[His inner spirit like a lion,]
[Not merely the great sage, Kök-Kashka,]
When he attacked the people of Beijing,
Bull-necked, camel-thighed,
Crushing whoever grappled with him,
Broad-legged, wide-chested,
Taking aim, biting his lip,
His two eyes red as embers,
Fire burning in the darkness,
The warrior's brow shone,
Tall of stature, broad of shoulder,
Strength befitting a warrior.
[That thief from the darkness,]
The swine who came from China,
May his deeds come to nothing.
[Devastating the people, driving off horses,]
[He was lacking in courage.]
Traveling at night, absent by day,
He was a creature of the night watch.
The raider who came from China,
Was the accursed one himself.
[Akjoltoy, seeing him from the side,]
Eagerly girding on his sword,
Taking a red-plumed spear,
Bellowing till ribs shook,
He called out to the great sage:
If you are a hero, if you are a lion,
I have caught up with you, great sage.
Over hills and hollows, broken roads,
I have hastened here, great sage,
[The black steel is leveled,]
[I have come pressing forward, great sage,]
[Are you a woman, so frail,]
Hurrying as you drive off wretched livestock?
For driving horses out of a valley,
You have begun imagining yourself a lion.
You excited, dog-cursed wretch,
You have begun posing as a warrior.
Now I shall see your true appearance,
Now I shall beat out your madness,
Your home is Beijing, a great nation,
Countless as black insects,
[Your appearance like dark wheat,]
I have come to strike at your life.
I have come to see your mettle,
I have come to learn your true nature,
[I shall test your strength.]
My name is Akjoltoy,
When an enemy advances fiercely,
[I myself am the dark abyss.]
When an enemy comes to clash,
I myself am a terrible calamity.
Why have you changed your appearance?
Foolishly driving off horses,
Why have you roused your madness?
Changing your look in anger,
[Why rage like one unbound?]
Wolves will tear at your belly,
Vultures will peck out your eyes.
You attacked first, madman,
[Ravens will hollow out your crown.]
Beijing was a people of asses,
Alone across many plains,
Saying you would make war on me,
You were the one I wished for.
Vowing an offering to Babedin,
Wishing to die in battle,
You were the one I wished for.
I had thought you a great sage,
You are a thieving sage,
I had thought you a heroic sage,
You are a worthless sage.
Wind-filled chest, cold snout,
You are a panicking sage,
If four mares fall into your hands,
You are a fleeing sage,
[Turning aside, your blood recoiling,]
You have come seeking shelter.
Through ravines, hills, and ridges,
[You have come to sift through them,]
A calamity your seven forefathers could not bear,
My sage, you have come to meet it,
[Without a thought or a plan,]
You are a panicked fool.
Stealing horses in the night,
You yourself are a fleeing fool.
You are the accursed one himself,
Of the witless Chinese,
[You are their dark watching eye.]
This was all your deed amounted to,
Karajoy and Kojojash,
Your fathers died together,
At the hands of the Kara-Kyrgyz tribes.
[This was the blood price of your fathers,]
Akjoltoy, son of the Kyrgyz,
Wreaks slaughter without idle quarrels,
He is no warrior to lie idle.
[The turmoil your seven forefathers passed through,]
[Do not ask how far I can reach.]
My name is Akjoltoy,
My battle cry is Kutubiy,
[He is khan of the mighty Kyrgyz.]
Turn back, great sage,
You too are a khan's son,
I too am a khan's son,
[While our heads are equal in rank,]
[God judges what is just,]
[Let me strike your equal down.]
You have come full of force,
Let me test my strength against yours.
While I have a warrior's head,
You raider who has invaded,
How could I surrender the livestock?
Without trading taunts and spear thrusts,
[Without grappling until fortune falls,]
How could I give up my livestock?
[Ala-Too, untouched by the cold,]
How dare you invade my land?
[Without earning any claim to that herd,]
How dare you raid my horses?
[Before you lies ground to be reaped,]
How dare you come to Talas?
I am Joltoy, the charging warrior,
Great in stature, fierce in fury,
The lion who comes prepared,
I have the hero Seytek as my khan,
I shall not dishonor my ruler,
I myself have strength to match you,
My name is Akjoltoy,
[My distinction is unique, my fury mighty,]
I alone am like countless troops,
If you ask my name, it is Joltoy,
Once you meet me, you will flee.
[If your usual madness seizes you,]
Go raid your own valley.
Sink into the earth rather than be a lord,
You belong among thieves.
Driving off horses in the night,
Is not the way of heroism.
[Utterly destroying your home,]
[Driving off your horses in a mass,]
I, Joltoy, am not one to be ruined,
[If you stir a quarrel without cause,]
You will not leave without turning to face me.
My name is Akjoltoy,
Listen well and carefully.
What smiths cannot find,
I am like keen red steel,
What falconers cannot find,
[I am like the bird my lord beheld,]
When we come face to face,
I myself am the dark scourge,
Who attacks countless hosts,
I am the leopard's eye,
You have met me and will die, great sage,
[Do not let your fiendish fury falter,]
While I have my head, I will not yield.
You have thoroughly raided my horses,
[I will not surrender them alive without a struggle.]
I am a lone warrior,
[I am the eye of an overwhelming host,]
If you would command, roar then,
Biting your finger, shaking your head,
Do not wail afterward,
[Let your glaring multitude come forth,]
I shall stand entirely alone,
If you would duel, come duel,
I shall stand alone against you all,
[Choose a ridge and name your pass,]
Name the place where you will fight firmly.
[While your equal still has his head,]
I will not give you the swift horse,
You have come forth full of force,
I will not yield to your strength.
If I stand tall in anger,
[I shall settle all your accounts,]
If I brace and gather my strength,
I shall beat out whatever madness you have.
Speak your words, leave no regrets,
Name the place where you will fight,
[Your possessions cannot simply be claimed,]
[Your foal is no match for my horse,]
Release my horses.
Talas is no easy land,
Ala-Too is no easy mountain pass,
[To be seized beneath an arm and overpowered,]
The Kyrgyz are no easy people.
[All your wisdom and laughter,]
Release my horses now,
I shall spill your blood like water,
I shall truly sap your strength,
[I shall cut your life to nothing,]
[Bringing pressure from your city,]
You obtained your khan's blessing,
[You thirsted and have drunk your fill,]
[Boasting of your prowess,]
[You have turned your hand to theft,]
I shall drain your strength,
I shall not rest until I spill your blood,
I shall reclaim my livestock!
So saying, Akjoltoy,
Seethed and fumed in anger,
Raging without pause,
He gritted his teeth fiercely.
[His glaring eyes changed,]
Frowning like a clouded day,
[His ruddy complexion turned ashen,]
His nostrils cold as ice,
[His exertion burned like embers,]
Preparing himself in wondrous ways,
No mortal stood to face him,
Both bloodthirsty and heroic,
A sage rich in wisdom,
His opponent was the great sage,
Such was the situation of their combat.
A warrior flourishing since childhood,
A warrior who knew the enemy's plans,
A sage rich in wisdom,
[He lunged from afar,]
A wise man of frank speech,
The wrestling champion, warrior Joltoy,
Would he refrain from battle?
Letting the enemy gain the advantage,
Would God forsake Joltoy?
And in Joltoy's hand,
A painted arrow tipped with steel,
Bending supple honeysuckle wood,
[Thinking it would serve through summer days,]
If an ill-fated hour should come,
[Lest it become soft and useless,]
[He had it worked at the forge,]
[Cutting brass in the heat of the coals,]
Steel was fitted to its tip,
[Four joined lengths in all,]
[So nothing struck could resist its bite,]
[The smith fashioned it close at hand.]
[A wondrous bow with moonlike limbs,]
Akjoltoy took it up,
[Binding to the target, shooting once,]
[Shooting a thousand in succession,]
Fit to carry at his side,
[The measure of his shoulder blades,]
When strength surged into his precious life,
The defense of his entrusted life,
[When extended, its base rang out,]
At its thud, life departed,
From his heroic forefather Kutu,
It had been left as an inheritance,
[When drawn, steel would snap,]
[Superior iron, apple-headed,]
It distinguished neither far nor near,
[If he prepared the Onogor,]
Used in earnest, it shattered the foe,
